structure: resident monologue in the toy box: the figure swaps heads and each head is a card cutting its own promo; the card-art animals of the toy box are the rest of the roster; ends on the jobber's only choice
bestOfReason: Heads 1-4: babyface, heel, tweener and the head from the package (the jobber).
The trick 9, 13, 14, 11: the box neighbours from the card art teach selling and its lies.
Fear 17, 22: the mask that stays on, the bag nobody opens.
Who decides 45, 46, 49: the spider in a suit, the cricket, the eye on the shelf.
Alone 30, 31: the empty box and the fake crowd on the wall.
Real 35, 55: the cracked head, the cop who writes him up.
Finish 41, 42, 56 + the jobber's choice (4, second beat).

orderReason: Deck order kept except: the oversell clown 11 comes after the stomp punch as the overdone counterexample; the jobber's power returns as the final card beat.

cards.cardText: The Babyface: high-flying moves, because audiences cheer for that. A slave to approval.
The Heel: brutal, sneaky moves. If they aren't booing, you aren't doing your job.
The Tweener: the audience decides to cheer for you on their own. You don't ask for it.

cardText: The Jobber: isolated and picked apart. You exist to make the other guy look good.
When defeated, you may choose who defeats you. That is your only control.

cards.cardText: The Master Seller: maintain the illusion of peril. Limp to the ring. Make them believe.
The Thigh Slap: slapping the thigh when kicking. A loud sound suggests impact. An audio lie.
The Stomp Punch: stomping on the mat when punching. Kinetic misdirection.
The Oversell Clown: reacting to an attack far beyond reality. A mockery of the sport.
The Sacred Mask: kayfabe sacred to their identity. The biggest identifier. Never remove it.
The Snake Bag: the bag has a live snake. Terrify them before the match starts.
The Booker: the ending is pre-planned. You are just a puppet.
The Spot Caller: calling moves in the ring. A basic outline, filled in with sweat.
The Hard Cam: if the camera didn't see it, it didn't happen.
The Empty Arena: taped in empty arenas, pausing for a pop that never comes. Surreal.
The Green Screen Crowd: a failed attempt to hide the emptiness. Audio sweetening on a lie.
The Real Injury: Goldberg's shoulder smashed into the ring-post. The crowd goes nuts: it's real.
The Kayfabe Police: protecting the business. Keep the secrets secret, or get fired.
The Finisher: the Leg Drop. The most important moment. If this hits, go home.
The False Finish: the art of the near-fall, kicking out at two point nine nine, crowd vertical.
The Retirement Match: leaning on the fourth wall. Rising, and falling. See you next season.
